issue_context.title: Datadog creates an executor job each state change event.
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Datadog creates an executor job each state change event
because `state_changed_listener` is run in the executor.

`influxdb`, `watson_iot`, and `zabbix` have examples of
how to avoid the frequent context switches by running
a separate thread and consuming the updates from a queue.

These integrations have not yet been updated to use `queue.SimpleQueue`
https://docs.python.org/3/library/queue.html#queue.SimpleQueue

New implementations should use this since we only support python
3.7 and later. 

Also, be sure to decorate the function that adds to the queue
with `@callback` so it does not run in the executor 

Examples: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/42265
